title: Suffix Copying Run
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let $y,r,\mathrm{pre},x,u$ be finite Boolean words with $y=\mathrm{pre}\,r$. Starting from the pair-loader configuration in state $3$, with physical input position $|\mathrm{pre}|+1$, input buffer $x$, choice buffer $u$, and buffer-head positions $|x|$ and $|u|$, after exactly $|r|$ steps the configuration is in state $3$, at physical input position $|y|+1$, with input buffer $x$, choice buffer $ur$, head positions $|x|$ and $|ur|$, and empty output.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
replaced: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic machine and let the physical input $y$ decompose as $y = p\,r$ for words $p$ and $r$. From the suffix-copy loader state at position $|p| + 1$ with buffers $x$ and $u$, exactly $|r|$ steps of the pair-loader machine append $r$ to the choice buffer, ending at the right boundary of $y$ with the input buffer $x$ unchanged and no physical output.
